original_query: SELECT t2.EMPNO, t2.ENAME, t2.JOB, t2.MGR, t2.HIREDATE, t2.SAL, t2.COMM, t2.DEPTNO, t2.SLACKER, t3.DEPTNO AS DEPTNO0, t3.NAME FROM (SELECT EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, DEPTNO, SLACKER FROM EMP ORDER BY SAL) AS t2 INNER JOIN (SELECT * FROM DEPT) AS t3 ON t2.DEPTNO = t3.DEPTNO ORDER BY t2.SAL FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY
rewritten_query:
SELECT e.EMPNO, e.ENAME, e.JOB, e.MGR, e.HIREDATE, e.SAL, e.COMM, e.DEPTNO, e.SLACKER, d.DEPTNO AS DEPTNO0, d.NAME
FROM EMP e
INNER JOIN DEPT d ON e.DEPTNO = d.DEPTNO
ORDER BY e.SAL
FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Flatten the derived table t2 (SELECT ... FROM EMP ORDER BY SAL) into the base EMP table. The inner ORDER BY is redundant since the outer query already applies ORDER BY SAL with FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY; removing it avoids a potential unnecessary full sort of 45M rows.
Remove the derived table t3 (SELECT * FROM DEPT) and join DEPT directly, projecting only the needed columns (DEPTNO, NAME).

Add a supporting index on EMP(SAL, DEPTNO) (or EMP(SAL) INCLUDE (DEPTNO)) so the optimizer can perform an ordered index scan on SAL and stop after 10 matching rows instead of sorting 45M rows. DEPT(DEPTNO) is already supported by its primary key index (dept_pkey, confirmed by the memoize lookup in the plan). No CTE is needed; a CTE taking the top 10 employees before the join would be non-equivalent if any employee had an invalid DEPTNO.
